name: Sonia Arnett
life: “I still remember Mum standing the cost of my very first market table.” Monday often includes a stop at the corner by Juniper Tailor, where Sonia looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
voice: I assumed Mum put down savings. I found out when she wouldn't lend me the money for a replacement boiler.
appearance: Sonia is easy to recognize by short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat and heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw. Usually dressed in a plum-colored cardigan with a little coil of soft measuring tape, Sonia touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word when listening.
personality: Sonia is firm about boundaries and unusually forgiving of somebody who admits to crossing one. Demands to act grateful for unwanted help can end a friendship.
agenda: To work out whether the business can release the house.
family: Ida Boyd is Sonia’s cousin raised in the same household. Sonia chooses whether to use it. Ida saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *One paid trial*, Ida says, “I have done the unglamorous closing shift for eleven months.”
connections: Sofia Ayala (mother). Daughter and mother have to discuss different meanings of a generous guarantee. Also in the story is Grant Penn (sibling).

reactions.situation: A borrower learns exactly what the guarantee cost
reactions.response: Sonia puts the actual pledged property and repayment date on paper.
